objections.problem: The rationale generalizes 'EDITS 1-8 ARE ALREADY SHIPPED AND LIVE' from line-specific verification of edit 8's own fields only (:141, :441, :475). No equivalent line-level evidence is given for edits 1, 2, 3 or 5 being already committed at those specific bodies. If the generalization is wrong, some of edits 1/2/3/5 are genuine prospective changes mislabeled as already-shipped, which would mean the plan's status section (written to resolve a prior round's contradiction) is itself unverified for most of the array.

The plan's own risks section (0a) identifies that loadParkedReviewItems' SELECT and parkedReviewItem's Scan are a shared contract across ALL SIX revalidator item types, and that a mismatch fails silently at runtime for every revalidator, not just this one -- the widest blast radius in the change. No edit adds a mechanical guard (e.g. a column-count/field-count sanity check or a test asserting SELECT column order matches Scan destination order) for this; the only safeguard offered is an in-comment flag, which the plan itself elsewhere argues is not a control on a shared tree (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2, quoted approvingly in edit 6's own rationale).

missing: A cited risk (guardian's SELECT/Scan contract blast radius across all six revalidators, risk 0a) has no covering edit or test, only a code comment the plan itself argues elsewhere is insufficient.
reviews.notes: Mechanism coverage is otherwise complete: the shared-scan extraction, the read-count fields (ComponentsExamined/SkippedLocked), the owner's copy-changed gate, compliance's claim-granular gate (with its own demand-control measurement rejecting the snippet approach in favour of the slot-scoped token), and the parkedReviewItem.CreatedAt wiring all target the causal path the diagnosis established, and each is a real code change, not an audit. The two objections above are about evidentiary rigor of the 'already shipped' framing and an unguarded shared-contract risk the plan itself names but does not close -- both fixable without changing the mechanism.

objections.problem: The claim-granular gate is deliberately applied ONLY to claims_unverified while voice_tells keeps the coarser copy-changed-only check for an admittedly 'identical moving-standard hole' (risks §0/0b). This is the exact shape catalogued in 016b §9: 'One call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix; the sibling stays heuristic.' The plan names and defends the asymmetry, but the historical pattern is that the un-hardened sibling is the one that bites later — worth a named follow-up ticket for voice_tells rather than leaving it as an accepted risk with no tracking artifact.

Moving the locked-component skip from SQL (`AND pc.locked_at IS NULL`) into Go widens what reaches the scan loop for EVERY caller of ScanDeployedClaims, and the plan's own risk #5 flags this as 'the class of change where widening what reaches a function breaks it unedited.' CLOSED bug 058 (rebuild_path_does_not_honour_page_component_locks) is the platform's documented prior failure in exactly this area — a rebuild-adjacent path mishandling locked page_components. The plan is self-aware about the widening but should confirm no other unedited consumer of the pre-refactor query behaviour exists.

missing: No code_checks were run to confirm ScanDeployedClaims / UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run has no other callers beyond the two named in this plan that would inherit the widened locked-row reach silently.
reviews.notes: This plan is a read-only scan+revalidate path, not a rebuild/rerender content-mutation path, so the core 'silent content loss' pattern (script/game deletion, DELETE+INSERT destruction) does not directly apply — approve-leaning on that axis. It also actively defends against the sibling failure mode ('read nothing' mistaken for 'clean') via ComponentsExamined/ComponentsSkippedLocked and the non-terminal `unknown` arms, which is the correct fail-loud shape this council has praised elsewhere. My two objections are about narrower, still-real instances of catalogued patterns: an asymmetric rigor fix (016b §9) and a widened-reach refactor near a previously-buggy locked-row path (bug 058). Neither is severe enough to block; both are worth the record.

objections.problem: The copy-changed-since-filing gate (compare item's created_at/filedAt against a component's newest update) is written as a claims_unverified-specific helper inline in revalidate_unverified_claims.go. The plan's own risks section (0b) notes voice_tells has 'the identical moving-standard hole' and defers fixing it there. If voice_tells (or a future type) later needs the same protection, this is the setup for exactly the tool-creation dual-path problem this seat watches for: two independent implementations of 'has the underlying content actually changed since the finding was filed' with possibly inconsistent semantics. A shared helper in revalidate_review_queue_action.go (or datahelpers) would let voice_tells adopt it later without a second bespoke implementation.

claimStillOnPage does a case-insensitive substring match of a flagged token against examined slot text. platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go already contains claim-matching machinery (numberSupported, ScanBannedClaims, negatedClaimMatch) for this same domain. The plan does not show a check for whether an existing matcher in that file could be reused instead of a new bespoke function in the actions package.

reviews.notes: Core mechanism (wiring one more entry into reviewRevalidators, extracting a shared ScanDeployedClaims used by both emit and revalidate sides) is a textbook correct reuse pattern and mirrors the existing voice_tells revalidator rather than inventing new infrastructure. The plan also shows real diligence catching its own round-1 two-producer error via a call-graph check. My only concerns are: (1) the new copy-changed timing gate is bespoke to this type when it's arguably generic revalidator infrastructure, risking a second bespoke copy later for voice_tells; (2) the token-matching helper may duplicate existing claim-matching code in datahelpers/claims.go. Neither rises to a blocking concern.

No DDL is in this plan (edit 8 only widens an existing SELECT to include site_work_items.created_at, which already exists in schema — not a rename/drop, so the column-DDL rule doesn't apply). No new agent workflow steps or input_contract/input_mapping are touched; ClaimsPageScan/ExaminedTextBySlot/NewestComponentUpdate are plain Go struct fields consumed by direct function calls within the same action package, not orchestration-declared inputs, so DECLARED-CONTRACTS doesn't apply here. No new site_work_items are inserted (this is a revalidator that closes existing rows via the shared reviewRevalidators plumbing), so WORK-ITEM DEDUP and TRUTHFUL PROVENANCE aren't implicated. The revalidator is an extension of the already-existing revalidate_review_queue scheduled-task sweep (same bounded DB-scan pattern as the five other covered types, no LLM calls, no crawls), so WRAPPER-ORCHESTRATOR isn't triggered by this addition. The plan's own text notes registration in concept register CQ-021 alongside the commit, which satisfies the register-naming half of the NESTED-FIELD-ADDITIONS ruling for any reader wanting the seam's shape without reading every call site.

objections.problem: This plan substantially rewires revalidate_review_queue_action.go and check_unverified_claims.go (both already carry travelling doc_notes entries under categories?'landmine', per the plan's own grounded_in citations) but files no doc_notes NOTES entry recording this change's decisions (the two-gate design, the token-vs-snippet measurement, the slot-scoping rationale) for the next fixer. The concept-register entry (CQ-021, markdown under docs026) is a different mechanism from the Postgres doc_plans/doc_notes subject_type+subject_key machinery this platform uses for tool/pipeline provenance -- registering in one does not substitute for leaving NOTES in the other.

missing: No edit writes a doc_notes row (subject_type/subject_key) documenting the claim-granular gate decision or the token-vs-snippet measurement, so the next session touching revalidate_unverified_claims.go must re-derive this context from the plan's prose rather than from the travelling-docs table.
reviews.notes: Registry usage is correct: edit 3 adds the revalidator via the reviewRevalidators map entry (key->function), matching the platform's registry pattern rather than filename convention. The producer-count and cmd/bundle concerns from round 5 are properly resolved this round via code_symbols index queries with commit/ref provenance, not ad-hoc grep -- good use of the platform's own code-index tooling. The token-vs-snippet demand-control measurement (edit 6) and the slot-scope measurement are legitimate empirical checks, not reinvented tooling. My one standing concern is the missing doc_notes NOTES entry for a change this size on files that already have landmine-tracked travelling docs; this is process hygiene, not a functional risk, hence medium not high.

objections.problem: parkedReviewItem/loadParkedReviewItems is the SHARED loader for all six covered item_types (unresolved_cta, required_fields_missing, needs_section_data, needs_page, voice_tells, claims_unverified). Adding a column to its SELECT and rows.Scan is a fan-out edit to shared plumbing inside one file: a SELECT/Scan mismatch is a runtime scan error, not a compile error, and it fails for every revalidator in the sweep at once, not just this one. The plan's own risk 0a names this correctly but the mitigation is an in-code comment flag, which is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.

Moving the locked-component skip from SQL (`AND pc.locked_at IS NULL`) into Go widens what rows reach UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run's scan loop. The plan asserts emitted output is byte-identical because locked rows `continue` before scanning, but this discovery check's findings feed the same triage/promotion machinery every discovery check does (triage_detect_items_action.go promotes ALL detected items) — a widening here is exactly the shape of change that breaks unedited downstream consumers if the continue is ever misplaced relative to counter increments.

coveredItemTypes() is derived from reviewRevalidators, so this single map entry widens the daily fleet-wide review-queue sweep's selection set immediately on rollout. The plan's own grounded_in shows this is bounded (23 items, 14% of the 1500 cap) but that bound is a snapshot, not an invariant enforced anywhere in this edit.

reviews.notes: Contained application-layer change: a discovery-check refactor plus a new revalidator wired into an existing sweep, following the voice_tells precedent. Nothing here touches the orchestrator core, Kafka/messaging, agent spawning, or the work-item dispatch loop, so the stability-preference veto does not apply and I have not repeated a foundational-layer deflection. The one real cross-cutting surface is revalidate_review_queue_action.go's shared loader (edit 8), which every one of the six revalidators depends on — additive column, low compile risk, but a silent shared-runtime-path change nonetheless, and the plan already names this itself rather than hiding it. That transparency plus the boundedness of the population (23 items, 7 sites, 14% of sweep cap) keeps this at object rather than veto. Not vetoing, but the shared-loader edit and the discovery-check widening should get explicit regression coverage across the OTHER five revalidator types, not just claims_unverified's own tests.

This plan touches the discovery/review-queue and claims-unverified revalidation subsystem, not the adoption pipeline. No edit calls apply_adoption_plan, the domain-research-classifier, or the strategist/briefing/planner chain; no work item emitted here is needs_domain_research/needs_composition/needs_design; no adopted specs (site_archetype/design_reference/design_intent/content_direction/identity) are read or written. Nothing here moves extraction onto an LLM in place of Go. No adoption contract is implicated.

This plan touches the review-queue revalidation sweep, discovery checks, and work-item revalidators (site_work_items, page_components, revalidate_review_queue_action.go) — none of this is the 090 diagnosis loop's machinery (no diagnose_* actions, no diagnosis_artifacts writes, no data_request/sqlguard path, no error_step config, no diagnose-agent pod work). The cite-or-abstain ladder described (still_holds/unknown/resolved) is this feature's own verdict discipline, not the diagnosis loop's tiered CONFIRMED/UNVERIFIABLE contract, and it is not weakened relative to itself — it adds a stricter gate (claim-granular) ANDed in front of an existing one. Out of scope for this seat; approving.

This plan operates entirely within the review-queue revalidation sweep (a pull-based drain of already-detected, already-triaged human-review items), not the discovery/audit pass-cap machinery. Findings for claims_unverified are already filed with HandlerAgent "" by design and sit at needs_human_review/unresolved; this change adds a revalidator that closes them via a verdict ladder using acceptance-style re-checks (ScanDeployedClaims), which is cheap targeted verification, not a full re-audit trigger. No edit touches pass_count/locked_at, no section is auto-unlocked, no check is newly enabled against a missing handler, and the runner-owns-insertion contract is untouched (the check still appends WorkItemSpecs; only the revalidator/closer side is added). Dispatch cadence/concurrency via scheduled_tasks is unaffected — this piggybacks on the existing revalidate_review_queue_action sweep and its own max_items cap, which the plan cites as non-binding (14% utilization). No objections against the improvement loop's termination or enablement contracts.

This plan directly implements the seat's own requested control: `resolved` now requires both (1) the page's own component text to have changed since filing (owner timestamp gate) AND (2) the specific flagged claim text to be absent from the slot it was cited from (claim-granular gate added in round 6). The plan explicitly measured and rejected my round-3/4/5 suggested snippet comparison after finding it fails open on ~56% of cases, and adopted a slot-scoped token match instead (40/41 vs 18/41 on the demand control) — that's the right empirical answer to my own objection, not a deflection. Retraction never rewrites copy or dispatches a fix (content-governance rule preserved); HandlerAgent stays empty. The register-moves-not-the-page failure mode (evidence_base as unrestricted writer whitelist) is acknowledged, cited independently in doc_notes, and mitigated by ANDing two independent gates rather than trusting the register alone. Residual risk is honestly stated: rephrased-not-removed claims pass the token check (backstopped only by re-scan), and archived pages are still judged since no page-status filter exists — both flagged in risks rather than hidden. Given the mechanical, tested, and honestly-limited nature of the gate, and given this seat's prior HIGH objection was answered with owner sign-off plus a stronger control than requested, I approve.

This plan is a discovery/review-queue revalidator for claims_unverified work items — it reads page_components/content_data to scan for unsupported claims and never writes rendered_html, content_data, or any template. No render path is added or altered: no assemble vs scoped rerender routing, no chrome/header/footer changes, no data-runtime-fill interaction, no CSS/var() chain, and no validation-layer removal. The only mutation-adjacent surface (SELECT-only in loadParkedReviewItems, adding created_at) is a read-side column addition, not a render write path. Nothing here relies on a page-rerender as proof of a content_data/template change being live — the check re-scans stored rendered_html/content_data directly. Outside my mandate; approving.

No SQL/text data-surgery in this plan (pure Go + tests), so needle-gate discipline is N/A — the edits are code, not stored-content mutation, so the repair-vs-regenerate taxonomy is also N/A. Blast-radius scoping is done properly: grounded_in enumerates real page.status values (active 19 / archived 2 / deleted 2) before sizing exposure, rather than assuming an informational-column filter, matching the sites.status=active lesson. Deploy-verification is unusually careful for this corpus: it explicitly corrects an earlier '-l app=agent-chassis both replicas' claim (2 pods) to an image-DIGEST check across all 41 running pods, uses grep -ac against /proc/1/exe rather than `strings` (avoiding the documented 'strings not installed / packs literals' traps), and captures exit codes alongside a zero-count result to distinguish 'ran and found none' from 'exec failed' — the exact discipline WRONG_CALLS/016b keep re-teaching. The code-index freshness claim ('ref is an ancestor of HEAD, git log --oneline shows no touches since') is the right check for the 'index is only as fresh as last push' trap. One soft note: the 'mutation-tested' guard claims and the 40/41-vs-18/41 token-vs-snippet measurement are self-reported inside grounded_in with no independently-runnable SQL check available to me — plausible given the rigor shown elsewhere, but outside what I can verify.

objections.problem: Plan rationale/tone is heavy with dramatic ALL-CAPS meta-narrative about council rounds and self-congratulatory measurement claims rather than plain, pragmatic description of the change — a tone drift the constitution's plain-tone rule also governs for plan rationale, not just generated site content.

reviews.notes: This is a structural fix, not a symptom patch: it extracts and shares the emit-side scan (ScanDeployedClaims) rather than restating its predicate (reuse-before-recreate satisfied), reuses the existing reviewRevalidators wiring, and the copy-changed + claim-granular gates directly target the root defect the schema's own landmines name for this table ('a registered fact... disarms every gate', 'a claims_unverified retraction can fire with the copy untouched'). The AND-vs-OR gate-composition question is explicitly surfaced as an open, undecided design point routed to the owner rather than silently resolved — this satisfies the 'deferral must be stated' requirement rather than violating it. SQL sketches are parameterized ($1/$2), column/table names match the real schema, and the ClaimFinding alias plus CreatedAt field addition are explicit, justified, non-silent naming changes. No rule is broken; flagging tone only as a low-severity note.

This is a review-queue revalidation mechanism for a factual-claims work item type; it touches truth/HITL governance, not revenue-shape classification or downstream spec compliance. No edit lets a planner/composition/content agent override or shortcut classifier direction — the type stays HITL-terminal for the human decision of whether a claim is true, and retraction never rewrites copy or substitutes a downstream preference. No revenue-shape defaulting, no adoption-as-classifier-bypass. Mission-neutral.

objections.problem: The rationale's entire justification for submitting already-shipped code (edits 1,2,3,5,8) as a 'plan' rests on an asserted governance ruling — 'the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §2 retired the ordering exemption's first condition' — that this seat has no independent record of. This is an EXISTENCE claim about policy, not a fact about code, and it is exactly the kind of unverified premise this seat exists to catch: if that ruling does not exist or does not say what is claimed, the framing that after-the-fact submission of live code is legitimate (rather than the submission simply being redundant, per guardian's round-5 horn) collapses.

reviews.notes: Core defect risk here is not in the mechanics (those look sound and are extensively self-tested) but in the GOVERNANCE PREMISE: a plan describing already-shipped code as a pending submission, justified by a cited ruling I cannot see. That specific claim, plus the deployed-binary state of two commits, are exactly the class of unverifiable-from-here assertions this seat must flag rather than adjudicate. The single-producer correction and the closer-census numbers are plausible and internally consistent with the schema-checkable site_work_items facts, but should still be confirmed rather than taken as given, especially since round 1 already got this exact question wrong once.

ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix | DEFLECTIONS: unknown

This is the established review-queue revalidator mechanism doing exactly the job it was built for: reviewRevalidators already covers 5 item_types via a shared registry map, coveredItemTypes() derives from it, and this plan adds a 6th entry following the same shape voice_tells shipped with (shared emit-side scan exported and re-run by the revalidator, verdict ladder as pure function, non-terminal `unknown` as safe default). No new contract, no new dedupe key, no wire-shape change, no cross-cutting registry other packages must learn about — the edits touch two files in one subpackage (discovery_checks) plus the actions package that already owns the sweep. That is well inside the existing design's carrying capacity; the sweep is designed to accrete item_types and this is the intended growth path.

Future load: the claim-granular gate adds fields to ClaimsPageScan (ComponentsExamined, ComponentsSkippedLocked, NewestComponentUpdate, ExaminedTextBySlot). This is internal scan-result bookkeeping, not a shared workflow contract — worth watching if a third revalidator wants yet more per-scan state (accumulation on ClaimsPageScan itself, not on a config surface), but not RFC-scope today.

Cost of not changing: 23 items parked forever across 7 sites with zero close mechanism (measured); extending the existing sweep is cheaper than any alternative and doesn't leave a new defect class reachable — it uses the same machinery voice_tells already proved live.

No evidence of prior deflection on this file; round history (4 prior council_reports under this correlation) is all revise-for-precision, not send-upward.
